title: Flame Photometry Alkali Metal Concentration Measurement
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D flame photometry lab using Three.js for measuring alkali metal concentrations in solution samples.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 6) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.3) and a point light above the workbench (intensity 0.8).
- Create a lab workbench as a large flat box (brown/wood color) centered at y=0.
- Model a flame photometer instrument on the workbench: a rectangular body (dark gray, ~1.2x1.8x0.8 units) with a cylindrical burner nozzle on top (radius 0.15, height 0.4), a small sample intake tube on the left side (thin cylinder), and a rectangular digital display panel on the front face (black with green text).
- Place a rack of 5 test tubes on the left side of the bench. Each test tube is a thin cylinder (radius 0.08, height 0.6) with colored liquid inside. The 5 samples are:
  - Sample 0: Sodium (Na) standard 10 ppm — yellow-tinted liquid
  - Sample 1: Sodium (Na) standard 50 ppm — deeper yellow liquid
  - Sample 2: Potassium (K) standard 20 ppm — light violet liquid
  - Sample 3: Potassium (K) standard 80 ppm — deeper violet liquid
  - Sample 4: Unknown sample — clear/white liquid
- Add a small label (sprite or plane with canvas texture) above each test tube showing its name.
- Model a flame above the burner nozzle using a cone or custom geometry with emissive material. The flame should be invisible initially and appear when the instrument is turned on.

INSTRUMENT BEHAVIOR:
- The flame photometer has an ON/OFF state toggled by clicking a power button (a small red cylinder on the front panel) or pressing 'P' key.
- When ON, the flame appears above the burner with a default blue color (natural gas flame). The digital display shows 'READY'.
- When OFF, the flame disappears and the display shows 'OFF'.

SAMPLE LOADING:
- Clicking a test tube selects it (highlight with emissive outline or brightness increase). The selected sample index is tracked.
- Pressing 'L' or clicking a 'Load Sample' DOM button aspirates the selected sample into the photometer. The sample tube on the instrument glows with the sample color briefly.
- When a sample is loaded and the instrument is ON, the flame color changes based on the metal:
  - Na samples: flame turns bright yellow (hex #FFD700)
  - K samples: flame turns violet/lilac (#9B59B6)
  - Unknown sample: flame turns yellow-orange (#FFA500) — it contains Na at ~35 ppm

MEASUREMENT:
- After loading a sample with the instrument ON, pressing 'M' or clicking 'Measure' DOM button triggers a measurement.
- The digital display shows a simulated emission intensity reading (arbitrary units):
  - Na 10 ppm → intensity 120
  - Na 50 ppm → intensity 580
  - K 20 ppm → intensity 95
  - K 80 ppm → intensity 370
  - Unknown → intensity 405
- Measurement takes 2 seconds (display shows 'MEASURING...' then the result).
- After measurement, the result is stored in a results array.

CALIBRATION CURVE:
- A DOM overlay panel on the right side shows a calibration chart (HTML5 Canvas 2D, 300x250px).
- As Na standards are measured, yellow dots appear on the chart (x=concentration, y=intensity).
- As K standards are measured, violet dots appear on the chart.
- When at least 2 standards of the same element are measured, a linear regression line is drawn through those points.
- When the unknown sample is measured, its intensity is plotted as an orange triangle, and the estimated concentration is calculated from the Na calibration line and displayed below the chart.

CONCENTRATION CALCULATION:
- Use linear interpolation/regression: for Na standards (10,120) and (50,580), slope = (580-120)/(50-10) = 11.5, intercept = 120 - 11.5*10 = 5.
- Unknown Na concentration = (405 - 5) / 11.5 ≈ 34.78 ppm. Display rounded to 1 decimal.

HUD / DOM ELEMENTS:
- Top-left: instrument status text ('Instrument: ON/OFF').
- Top-right: 'Selected Sample: [name]' text.
- Buttons below the 3D canvas: 'Power (P)', 'Load Sample (L)', 'Measure (M)', 'Reset (R)'.
- Right panel: calibration chart canvas and concentration result text.
- Pressing 'R' resets all measurements, clears the chart, turns off the instrument, and deselects samples.

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- instrumentOn: boolean
- selectedSampleIndex: number (-1 if none)
- loadedSampleIndex: number (-1 if none)
- flameColorHex: string (current flame color hex, e.g. '#0000FF' for blue default)
- displayText: string (current text on the digital display)
- measuredResults: array of objects [{sampleIndex, intensity, element}]
- naStandardsMeasured: number (count of Na standards measured)
- kStandardsMeasured: number (count of K standards measured)
- calibrationSlope: number|null (Na calibration slope after 2 Na standards)
- calibrationIntercept: number|null
- unknownConcentration: number|null (calculated ppm, null until computed)
- measurementInProgress: boolean
- flameVisible: boolean
- sampleNames: array of 5 strings

OrbitControls should be enabled for camera rotation. Ensure all interactions work via both keyboard shortcuts and DOM buttons.
physics_constraints: Linear calibration: intensity = slope * concentration + intercept. For Na: slope=11.5, intercept=5. Unknown concentration derived from inverse: conc = (intensity - intercept) / slope ≈ 34.78 ppm. Emission intensities must be deterministic per sample. Flame color must correspond to the alkali metal element in the loaded sample.
